data.name: SeaBed
data.detailed_description:
Audio Novel Collection Bundle Now Available!

Complete the Audio Novel Collection to unlock the 4th Extra Episode for free!


Acerca do jogo

SeaBed is a critically acclaimed yuri-themed psychological mystery visual novel told through the perspectives of three separate characters: Mizuno Sachiko, a designer plagued by hallucinations of her past lover; Narasaki Hibiki, Sachiko's friend and a psychiatrist researching the workings of human memories; and Takako, Sachiko's former lover who has been rapidly forgetting her past, including how or why the two women drifted apart despite being together since childhood.

All three live in different worlds, but seek the same goal. To separate truth from illusion. To make sense of their own lives.

The Steam version of SeaBed has been updated to natively support 1440x1080 resolution.

Characters:

"At times, I'd wake up at night and hear all the sounds around me as if they were amplified. I'd feel like my head could burst at any second."

Although she moved to Tokyo straight after graduating university in order to seek employment, Mizuno Sachiko soon quit her job to establish Clover Design with her childhood friend Takako, becoming its young CEO.

Her main hobby is reading, but only because nothing else manages to interest her. Although Sachiko used to be quite an avid reader during her school years, finding a job means she now only opens a book every once in a while, whenever her schedule allows it.

After meeting Takako – an inexhaustible source of enthusiasm, as well as a stark contrast to her own personality – during her childhood years, Sachiko’s interests began to shift to whatever the other woman was doing at a given time.

"This is as good a time as any, so let's check it out."

Endlessly interested in and enthusiastic about the world, Takako gives the impression of a woman perpetually stuck in her childhood.

She fell in love with Sachiko at first sight back when they first met at the age of five. However, she does not identify as a homosexual, stressing that Sachiko simply happened to be a woman.

Takako discovers that she suffers from developmental amnesia, a condition that severely impairs her ability to recall many of her memories.

"I just like observing people."

A psychiatrist at Narasaki Mental Clinic. She was Sachiko's classmate and friend during her elementary school years, but the two drifted apart as they enrolled in different middle schools. After learning that Sachiko has been experiencing hallucinations, she takes it upon herself to treat her.

She is extremely picky about her brand of coffee, perhaps because the beverage serves as her sole companion during those long hours spent immersed in research.

Though not religious, she is a strong believer that everything happens for a reason, and all things have their place and order in the grand scheme of the world.

reviews.review:
I've just completed SeaBed and I find it hard to describe how I felt after into words while making sure to avoid spoilers. In short Seabed is one of the more interesting visual novels I've read. I can highly recommend this game and would also strongly advice going in to this blind. The slice of life story is slow and mundane at first notice but it'll soon develop into something far greater than it seems, which is why people don't mention most of the game to avoid giving out spoilers.

It's a yuri story about 2 best friends, along with a childhood friend of theirs spend their day to day lives traveling and at their day jobs. It's a linear story with no branching choices. The story is pretty much grounded focusing on slice of life scenarios of the characters. While the pacing is slow as we see the life events of the characters I did find a lot of charm in this slower and more relaxed storytelling. However as the story progress you'll slowly learn that there is much more going on underneath the wholesome narrative. After the prologue you'll learn some information that will completely change your perspective on how you'll perceive the events before and after the prologue. Despite going through the many slice of life story telling, if you are observant enough you will be able to pick up some details that does not add up in the narrative. This game is marketed as a psychological mystery VN after all and the main mystery is about uncovering the truth to the lives of the 3 protagonists. The story does not narrate events in order, constantly jumping between time, locations and perspectives. It does get confusing but it also helps to convey the mysterious nature of the plot to the player. As you read the story you'll get to know the characters more and more through one life event after another. All while you were trying to theorize what really happened using the various information you've learned from your observations. It is a slow burn of a narrative. It may start out mundane at first but it does delve into heavy subjects like memories, love, mental health, social dilemma and much more from time to time. It will all accumulates to a resolution that really pays off your experience of going through this one beast of a story. I won't share any more detail than this but just know that in the end you'll look back and felt that even the mundane activities in their lives are as important for the characters. Not a single moment was wasted here.

Besides that there are a few details I really like about this game. The presentation is definitely unique compared to most conventional VNs. The story text takes up the entire screen overlaying on top of the visuals behind, and the dialogue of the characters are shown line by line from top to bottom. The story is always told through the perspective of one character, usually with their name shown at the bottom left. This meant that you will be experiencing the events first hand as the characters do. Pairing with this UI it really helps to put the player into the character's perspective. Especially with most of the background are photographed in the perspective of how one person would view these locations. It is definitely a refreshing experience if you are used to traditional VN UI. However, it does make keeping track of who is which line harder to track since there is no obvious indication for who is saying a line. I also like how the portraits and CG are drawn. It's definitely not professional standard anime art, the line work and rendering are pretty soft, but it stands perfectly with the melancholy tone of the story. While there is some fan service scenes here and there, they are few and far between and it was never meant to be there for the sake of fan service alone. The audio while mainly sourced from 3rd party assets, all the BGMs fit together cohesively and always matches the mood of the scene. The sound designs where very well done as well with most sound effects where added to help giving the scenes a bit more life.

With that said I however had a few complaints about the game though:
1. There are exactly 2 (or 3 depending on your preference) horrific jumpscares in game which definitely soured my experience. I get they want to convey a scary tone to the player at time but there are better ways to do so than cheap jumpscares.
2. The ending while being intentionally open for the player's interpretation, I do wish they expanded the narrative on the characters as they live their lives at least a little bit more after the ending. After learning about these characters for so long it's kind of sad not knowing how they managed their future.
3. I did find that there's still some questions left unanswered from the narrative after completing the game. Perhaps this was intentional, who knows. The whole plot is meant to be vague on purpose but not everything gets resolved cleanly.
4. The tips are not exactly well explained. They are basically extra scenes on top of the main story line that may spill more details about the character lives and overall mystery of the narrative. While it was recommended to play them as soon as you unlocked them, but my personal recommendation is read all of the tips you've unlocked right before you start chapter 10.

With that said, I would highly recommend giving this game a shot especially if you like slow melancholy narrative that focuses on the living in the moment and along with love ones. This is Paleontology first (and only as of the writing of this) VN and I enjoyed every moment of it, while the doujin circle had been quiet now I wish them the best of luck in their future endeavors.
